evidence.curator_note: Book draws 4 arc(s); moves <1,2,3,4> are drawn, move <5> is an implicit hook required for electron balance (not drawn on the page). ARC GEOMETRY AS READ FROM THE SCAN (zoomed to 14x): (1) a long arc whose tail sits on the CH=+OCH3 double bond and whose head points down-left into the empty space between the CH3O oxygen and that CH -- the forming O-C bond; (2) an arc whose tail is on the CH3O-CH2 bond and whose head points up-right into the SAME space, so two heads meet on the forming O-C bond; (3) a second arc from the CH3O-CH2 bond whose head points down-right onto the middle of the H2C-CH bond; (4) an arc whose tail is on the CH-CH (vertical) bond and whose head points down-left onto the same H2C-CH midpoint -- the two heads there make the characteristic 'W'. Two heads per new bond means single-electron arcs, so all four are encoded with electron_count 1. THE IMPLICIT FIFTH HOOK: as drawn, the C=+O pi bond gives up one electron (arc 1) and the C-C bond gives up only one (arc 4), yet the product the book prints, CH3O-CH=+OCH3, still has a full C=O and no C-C bond. The balance is restored by exactly one further single-electron move -- the second electron of the breaking C-C bond returning into the C=+O pi system -- which the book does not draw. It is encoded here as move 5. SUBSTRATE: the drawing is CH3O-CH2-CH(OCH3)-CH=+OCH3 (C6H13O3+, m/z 133.09), a permethylated-carbohydrate oxocarbenium; the products drawn are CH2=CHOCH3 and CH3O-CH=+OCH3 (m/z 75).

NO MØD RULE IS CROSS-LINKED, and this was CHECKED, not assumed (convention E). rule_index.json 'by_equation' has no '8.119' key at all -- its chapter-8 index runs 8.1-8.14 only (German-edition numbering), so nothing in src/data_generation/rules/ is authored for this equation. The nearest candidates in the set are the even-electron oxonium rules IMS_8_11 ('Field Rule 8.11 rH') and IMS_8_12 ('8.12 ind'), which were CHECKED by reading their DFS strings out of rule_index.json (no RDKit run was needed - the patterns are decisive). IMS_8_11 is '[C]1([H]2)([H]3)([H]4)[C]5([H]6)([H]7)[O+]8{=}[C]9([H]10)([H]11) >> [C]1([H]2)([H]3)[C]5([H]6)([H]7) . [H]4[O+]8{=}[C]9([H]10)([H]11)' and IMS_8_12 is NOT the same left-hand side -- the first draft of this note said it was, and that is corrected here against the rule source. IMS_8_12 is '[C]1([H]2)([H]3)([H]4)[C]5([H]6)([H]7)[O+]8{=}[C]9([H]10)[C]11([H]12)([H]13)([H]14) >> [C]1([H]2)([H]3)([H]4)[C+]5([H]6)([H]7) . [O]8{=}[C]9([H]10)[C]11([H]12)([H]13)([H]14)': its oxocarbenium carbon carries ONE H plus a methyl, not two H, and it cleaves heterolytically to [C+]5 plus the neutral carbonyl. Neither left-hand side matches this substrate, so the conclusion is unchanged. Both require a CARBON chain C1-C5 on the single-bonded side of the oxonium oxygen; in this substrate that position is the O-methyl (map 9), which has no further carbon, so neither left-hand side even matches. More fundamentally, one transfers a hydrogen and the other simply heterolyses the C-O bond; neither forms a NEW bond between a remote alkoxy oxygen and the oxocarbenium carbon, which is the whole content of Equation 8.119. Neither is a match; nothing else in the set migrates a heteroatom substituent.
